newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins fall on freeze worries.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins fall on freeze worries.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds fell in nervous early trading on fears further bonds could have been frozen, dealers said on Tuesday.

Dealers said on Monday that prices fell by at most 1.5 big figures amid rumours that some banks had been advised that some of their MinFins, totalling more than $50 million face value, had been frozen.

A Russian police officer working on a frozen MinFin case told Reuters on Monday that a large volume of Russian MinFin bonds may have been frozen this May in addition to the $24 million previously reported.
Officials from Finance Ministry, the bond issuer, and Vneshtorgbank, the main MinFin depositary, were not immediately available for comment.
"Almost nobody is trading now as there is no precise information," Avtobank dealer Alla Zakharova said.
Sberbank dealer Pavel Sool said many banks had stopped quoting prices in early trading, otherwise selling was mainly seen in the fourth and fifth tranches.
